content: Compass Community Services is a non-profit organization based in San Francisco, California, dedicated to providing a range of support services to homeless and extremely low-income families. Through its four programs—Clara House, Compass Family Center, Connecting Point, and Tenderloin Childcare Center—the organization serves over 3,000 clients annually. Originally established in 1914 as Travelers Aid San Francisco, the organization initially aimed to assist newcomers to the city, particularly young women and girls drawn by the Panama-Pacific International Exposition in 1915. Over the years, the organization has adapted its services to meet the needs of various populations, including stranded travelers, refugees, and homeless families. Despite the diversity of the groups served, the common thread has been the need for support in navigating the challenges of an often inhospitable urban environment. In 1976, the agency recognized the growing demand for respite childcare among families utilizing its services and responded by opening the Tenderloin Childcare Center (TLC). By 1990, TLC became the first licensed childcare center in San Francisco to reserve spaces exclusively for homeless children and those from extremely low-income families. Research indicates that homeless children experience developmental delays at four times the rate of their peers, with nearly 50% facing emotional challenges such as anxiety and depression. In 2002, TLC moved into its own dedicated building, enabling the center to enroll 72 children and, for the first time, offer care for infants. This specialization allows TLC to promptly identify and address developmental and emotional issues in its students. In response to the escalating crisis of family homelessness, the agency launched the Compass Family Center (CFC) in 1990. This program provides emergency shelter, counseling, referrals, and assistance in securing permanent housing for homeless families. Homeless families represent the fastest-growing segment of the homeless population in the United States, with children and families accounting for 40% of this demographic. In 1995, CFC expanded its services to include aftercare, pre-employment support, and psychotherapy. In 2006, the program received a three-year grant from the SF First Five Commission to implement the Positive Parenthood Project, which aims to improve developmental outcomes for children aged 0-5 through parent-child services. In 2007, CFC partnered with Catholic Charities CYO to launch SF HOME, a program providing housing subsidies to families who are homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness. This initiative aligns with the housing first principle, which prioritizes rapid rehousing or housing retention to prevent families from entering the cycle of homelessness. SF HOME also offers intensive support to help families increase their income through employment and training. In 1995, Compass Community Services established Clara House, a long-term supportive housing program. This initiative offers families the opportunity to live in a stable, service-enriched environment for up to two years while preparing for independent permanent housing. Initially, the program faced criticism from homeless advocacy groups due to a proposed requirement for families to provide proof of legal immigration status, a stipulation influenced by California's Proposition 187. This law barred undocumented individuals from accessing publicly funded employment services, a key component of Clara House. Given that a quarter of the program's funding came from the City of San Francisco, there were legal uncertainties about serving undocumented clients. Ultimately, the program decided to remove the legal status requirement for admission. Also in 1995, at the request of and with funding from the San Francisco Human Services Agency, the organization launched Connecting Point (CP). This program serves as the central intake and assessment center for families in San Francisco seeking access to the city's shelter system. In 2007, CP partnered with the Eviction Defense Collaborative to provide rental assistance, helping families maintain their housing and avoid homelessness.
